links.outcome: Detection sensitivity under simulated CT acquisition variation (dose, slice thickness, kernel)
links.effect: Baseline sensitivity 84.8%; soft kernel 74.3% (-10.5 pp), 5 mm slice 71.6% (-13.2 pp), 25% dose 76.0% (-8.8 pp), 50% dose 80.0% (-4.8 pp), 3 mm slice -2.4 pp (p=0.009).
links.quote: Soft kernel and 5 mm slice thickness produced the largest decreases: 74.3% (-10.5 pp, p < 0.05) and 71.6% (-13.2 pp, p < 0.05), respectively.

links.outcome: Sensitivity variation across acquisition parameters mimicking site/scanner differences
links.effect: Sensitivity fell from 84.8% baseline to 71.6-80.0% across simulated acquisition conditions, with slice thickness and soft kernel causing the largest drops.
links.quote: Slice thickness and soft reconstruction kernel represent stronger constraints on AI detection performance than image noise under these conditions.

unlisted_practices: Physics-guided simulation of acquisition parameter variation for post-deployment acquisition QA

screen.reason: Evaluates AI nodule detection model robustness across simulated clinical acquisition variations (dose reduction, slice thickness, kernel) to provide a practical framework for post-deployment imaging acquisition quality assurance.

primary.practice: acquisition parameter stress testing / post-deployment acquisition QA
